claims.text: The ARC dataset contains 7,787 grade-school science questions, split into a Challenge Set of 2,590 questions and an Easy Set of 5,197 questions.
Leading neural baseline QA models do not score significantly higher than a random baseline (25.02%) on the ARC Challenge Set.
The ARC Corpus contains 14 million science-related sentences relevant to approximately 95% of the ARC Challenge Set questions.
The DGEM model achieved a test score of 27.11% on the ARC Challenge Set and 58.97% on the Easy Set.
The BiDAF model achieved a test score of 26.54% on the ARC Challenge Set and 50.11% on the Easy Set.

evidence.description: The ARC Dataset consists of a collection of 7787 natural science questions... partitioned into a Challenge Set (2590 questions)... and an Easy Set (5197 questions).
none of the algorithms score significantly higher than the random baseline on the Challenge set, where the 95% confidence interval is ±2.5%.
The ARC Corpus, in fact, appears to mention knowledge relevant to approximately 95% of the ARC Challenge questions (from an analysis of a random sample of questions).
DGEM scored 27.11% on the Challenge Set test partition and 58.97% on the Easy Set test partition.
BiDAF scored 26.54% on the Challenge Set test partition and 50.11% on the Easy Set test partition.

methodologies.name: ARC Question Set Filtering and Partitioning
methodologies.description: Filtering multiple-choice science questions into a Challenge Set and Easy Set using an Information Retrieval solver and a Pointwise Mutual Information solver.
conditions: Incorrectly answered by both IR and PMI solvers using Waterloo corpus

methodologies.name: Multiple-Choice QA Adaptation via Entailment
methodologies.description: Converting multiple-choice questions into hypothesis assertions, retrieving premise sentences, and evaluating answer options using neural textual entailment models.

limitations.text: Earlier reading comprehension datasets (SQuAD, MCTest) contained questions solvable via surface-level cues alone.
Synthetic datasets like bAbI risk allowing models to reverse-engineer generation idiosyncrasies without advancing reasoning.
Standard IR retrieval methods bias toward sentences that match the whole question, failing to retrieve sentences that individually match partially but combine to answer the question.
Converting questions to hypothesis statements using simple fill-in-the-blank rules can yield non-grammatical sentences.

future_work.text: Develop more sophisticated rule-based or learned methods to convert question-answer pairs into grammatical assertions.
Develop advanced retrieval strategies and reasoning methods capable of combining multiple partial facts from separate sentences.
